lead_in: Name any two of these promises:
question_text: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.

official_answers.text: Give up loyalty to other countries
Obey the laws of the United States
Serve (help, do important work for) the nation (if needed)
Be loyal to the United States

why_it_matters.text: The Oath is the final step of becoming a citizen — a public promise to defend the Constitution, obey U.S. laws, and put loyalty to the United States above any other country. It's not just paperwork. It's the moment a person stops being a guest in this country and starts being a member of it. From that moment on, this nation is theirs.

fun_fact.text: New citizens take their Oath of Allegiance at a public ceremony — at a courthouse, or sometimes inside the National Archives in front of the actual Constitution and Bill of Rights. A version of this oath has been said by new Americans since 1790. That's over 235 years of welcoming new citizens to the United States.
